title: England drops Carse from Pakistan Test squad as investigation begins
dek: England fast bowler Brydon Carse has been removed from the squad for the second Test against Pakistan while the Cricket Regulator investigates footage of him in police handcuffs outside a bar in Derby on August 22, 2026. Carse becomes the third England player benched this summer for a disciplinary issue. The incident occurred less than 48 hours before he was scheduled to join the squad.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Carse, who has taken 58 wickets since his Test debut in October 2024 (more than any other England bowler in that span), was filmed in handcuffs outside a Derby bar on August 22 and removed from the Pakistan Test squad pending an investigation.
bottom_line: The investigation timeline and its findings will determine whether Carse faces formal sanction beyond squad removal. Watch whether Potts or Stokes face investigation or discipline given their presence in the footage, and whether a pattern of summer disciplinary breaches prompts Root to reintroduce conduct guidelines.
body: Brydon Carse has been removed from England's squad for the second Test against Pakistan while the Cricket Regulator investigates an off-field incident in Derby on August 22, 2026. The fast bowler becomes the third England player benched this summer for a disciplinary breach, testing the team's conduct standards just days after the captain called for improved behavior.

The 31-year-old was filmed in police handcuffs outside a bar in Derby on Saturday night, according to BBC Sport's reporting. Derbyshire Police confirmed that a man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly in Derby city centre and was de-arrested shortly afterwards after agreeing to leave the area. The Cricket Regulator, which received a referral from the ECB, has opened an investigation into the events.

Carse was scheduled to arrive in London within 48 hours to join the England squad for the second Test at Lord's. Instead, the ECB issued a statement: "Brydon Carse will no longer be available for selection for the second men's Test while this investigation is ongoing and the full facts are obtained." He has been replaced by 23-year-old Sonny Baker, who won his only Test cap in the second match of the series against New Zealand in June. The incident occurred as Carse was released from the first Test squad to play for Durham away at Derbyshire, a game the Division Two leaders won on Saturday evening.

Matthew Potts, Carse's Durham team-mate, was also in the footage from the incident; Ben Stokes could be seen in the background, according to BBC Sport's reporting. Footage of the three men circulated widely on social media.

Carse is the third England player to miss a Test this summer for a disciplinary reason. In June, Stokes and Gus Atkinson were present in a London nightclub when a member of England's security staff was struck by a Saracens rugby player, per BBC Sport's reporting. Both men missed the second Test against New Zealand while the incident was investigated and were eventually given a written warning. Stokes and Atkinson breached a team curfew that was introduced following late-night incidents during the winter. When Joe Root took over as England captain, replacing Stokes, he removed the curfew and relaxed guidelines on alcohol consumption around matches and in public.

On the day before the first Test against Pakistan, Root called on his players to be "really good role models and good human beings," telling BBC Sport: "You always want to represent your country in the best possible light. We might have fallen short of that on a few occasions in the recent past." England won that first Test by an innings inside three days at Headingley.

Since making his Test debut in October 2024, Carse has taken 58 wickets, more than any other England bowler in that span, per BBC Sport's reporting. In summer 2024, he was given a three-month ban for historical betting offences. The brief carries no statement from Carse or his representatives on the Derby incident.
